newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian local elections attract few candidates.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian local elections attract few candidates.

text.p: Most of the candidates in next month's Egyptian local council elections will win their seats and the level of interest in the contest is even lower than usual, political sources said on Thursday.

The liberal Wafd Party, one of the largest opposition groups, is boycotting the elections in the expectation that they would be rigged and most Islamists have turned down the chance to stand as independents for similar reasons, they said.

Partial figures published in government newspapers on Thursday showed that for 22,142 seats, about half of the total at stake, only 26,542 people had registered as candidates by the closing date earlier this week.
The ruling National Democratic Party of President Hosni Mubarak and like-minded independents account for the vast majority of the candidates in the elections, set for April 6.
The Wafd based its decision to boycott on its experience in the parliamentary elections of 1995, widely described as the dirtiest and most violent in Egyptian history.
The courts cancelled the results in more than 100 constituencies but parliament, which under the constitution has the last word on electoral disputes, ignored the court rulings.
Some of the Islamists who might have stood have been detained or jailed as part of the government's crackdown on the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood and its sympathisers.
The government said the parliamentary elections were free and fair and that the local elections will be so too.
The old local councils were dissolved last year after the courts ruled that the voting method, which gave all the seats in a council to the winning party, was unconstitutional.
